data.narrative:
Carbon Robotics is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Paul Mikesell that has raised $177M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 peers—1 public and 8 private companies in the robotics and manufacturing sector at the same or adjacent funding stages, including Hadrian, Nimble Robotics, Exotec, and Dexterity.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $177M total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C to subsequent-stage advancement, implies a valuation of $301M. Peer-median analysis across five same-sector comparables (Exotec at $2.0B, Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B, Dexterity and Hadrian each at $1.6B, and Nimble Robotics at $1.0B) yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.0B.

The two methods produce a wide spread, reflecting uncertainty inherent in early-stage robotics valuations. The triangulated analysis supports a range of $256M (floor) to $1.9B (ceiling), with a median of $975M. Key uncertainties include the appropriate comparability of peer companies given the heterogeneity of robotics subsectors, the relevance of later-stage peer valuations to a Series C company, and the extent to which raised capital reflects fair market valuation versus dilution dynamics in this nascent sector.
